dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Nam, have you heard of Amelia Earhart?
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, hæv juː ˈhɜːrd əv əˈmiːliə ˈɛrhɑːrt?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: The pilot? Yes. She disappeared in 1937, didn't she?
dialogue.reading: ðə ˈpaɪlət? ˈjɛs. ʃiː ˌdɪsəˈpɪrd ɪn ˈnaɪntiːn ˈθɜːrti ˈsɛvən, ˈdɪdənt ʃiː?

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Yes, over the Pacific Ocean. They never found any trace of her plane.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, ˈoʊvər ðə pəˈsɪfɪk ˈoʊʃən. ðeɪ ˈnɛvər ˈfaʊnd ˈɛni ˈtreɪs əv hɜːr ˈpleɪn.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: So she must have crashed into the sea.
dialogue.reading: soʊ ʃiː mʌst hæv ˈkræʃt ɪntə ðə ˈsiː.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: That's the most common theory. She was probably lost at sea.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ðə ˈmoʊst ˈkɑːmən ˈθɪri. ʃiː wʌz ˈprɑːbəbli ˈlɔːst ət ˈsiː.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: No. Some people think she might have landed on a small island.
dialogue.reading: ˈnoʊ. sʌm ˈpiːpəl ˈθɪŋk ʃiː maɪt hæv ˈlændɪd ɑːn ə ˈsmɔːl ˈaɪlənd.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Then someone might have seen her.
dialogue.reading: ˈðɛn ˈsʌmwʌn maɪt hæv ˈsiːn hɜːr.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Maybe. Others think she was taken by soldiers.
dialogue.reading: ˈmeɪbi. ˈʌðərz ˈθɪŋk ʃiː wʌz ˈteɪkən baɪ ˈsoʊldʒərz.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Well, she can't have disappeared without a reason.
dialogue.reading: ˈwɛl, ʃiː ˈkænt hæv ˌdɪsəˈpɪrd wɪˈðaʊt ə ˈriːzən.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Of course not. But it's still one of the greatest unexplained mysteries of the twentieth century.
dialogue.reading: əv ˈkɔːrs ˈnɑːt. bʌt ɪts ˈstɪl ˈwʌn əv ðə ˈɡreɪtɪst ˌʌnɪkˈspleɪnd ˈmɪstəriz əv ðə ˈtwɛntiəθ ˈsɛntʃəri.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I'd love to know what really happened.
dialogue.reading: aɪd ˈlʌv tə ˈnoʊ ˈwʌt ˈriːli ˈhæpənd.
